newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan opposition says no reforms, no elections.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan opposition says no reforms, no elections.

text.p: Kenyan opposition members of parliament on Friday threatened to disrupt elections due later this year unless President Daniel arap Moi enacts sweeping constitutional reforms.

The latest stand by the opposition came a day after Moi, 73 and in power for the last 19 years, hardened his stance and lambasted Western nations for urging dialogue to end the east African nation's political stalemate.

At a news conference in Nairobi, 11 opposition MPs blamed Moi for the political unrest which rocked Kenya on Monday and Wednesday and appealed to the business community to join efforts to force him to enact changes.

"In order to force the government to effect the necessary constitutional and legal reforms Kenyans should ensure by all necessary means at their disposal that the general elections are not held before reforms are effected," said the MPs in a joint statement.
James Orengo, deputy leader of the opposition, warned Moi of a rebellion similar to that which ended Mobutu Sese Seko's rule in Zaire unless the president gave in to the clamour for reforms.

"We are saying no reforms, no elections. We are committed to an extent that we will ensure there are no elections. Kenyans have the capacity to make this country ungovernable. We are in the begining of a revolution," Orengo added.

Nine people died in the unrest on Monday when the opposition called for rallies to press Moi into reforms. Further violence erupted on Wednesday when university students clashed with police and the paramilitary force.

The violence was the worst since Kenya returned to pluralist politics in 1991. The opposition wants Moi to allow free access to the media, overhaul of the state appointed Electoral Commission and a repeal of a colonial act which regulates political assemblies.
